This paper presents a comprehensive review of the current state of AI in medical imaging and identifies key challenges and opportunities for future development. The paper also outlines guiding principles and consensus recommendations for ensuring the safety, reliability, and ethical use of AI in medical imaging. These principles include transparency, accountability, fairness, privacy, and security, as well as the need for ongoing monitoring and evaluation of AI systems. The paper concludes by emphasizing the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and stakeholder engagement in developing and implementing trustworthy AI in medical imaging.

row.title: FUTURE-AI: Guiding Principles and Consensus Recommendations for Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence in Future Medical Imaging
row.prompt: Write the abstract for the academic paper titled "FUTURE-AI: Guiding Principles and Consensus Recommendations for Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence in Future Medical Imaging".
row.generation: The development of artificial intelligence (AI) has revolutionized various industries, including healthcare. With its potential to improve medical imaging accuracy and speed, AI is increasingly being integrated into clinical workflows for image analysis and interpretation. However, concerns arise about the reliability and trustworthiness of AI systems in this setting. In this paper, we outline guiding principles for building trustworthy AI in future medical imaging using consensus recommendations from a group of experts in the field. Our framework considers multiple dimensions such as data quality, model transparency, human oversight, ethical implications, and patient privacy. We also propose guidelines on how to measure and evaluate AI performance, validate models on new datasets, and incorporate knowledge exchange between humans and machines. These recommendations provide practical insights that can help ensure the responsible use of AI technologies with high stakes, ultimately leading to better outcomes for patients and improving healthcare delivery.

row.title: EdgeFlow: Achieving Practical Interactive Segmentation with Edge-Guided Flow
row.prompt: Write the abstract for the academic paper titled "EdgeFlow: Achieving Practical Interactive Segmentation with Edge-Guided Flow".
row.generation: EdgeFlow is a novel interactive segmentation method that utilizes edge-guided flow to achieve practical and efficient segmentation of images. The method is designed to handle complex and dynamic scenes, where traditional segmentation techniques may struggle. Edge-guided flow is used to guide the segmentation process by identifying and tracking edges in the image. This allows for more accurate and precise segmentation, even in the presence of noise and occlusions. The method is also designed to be interactive, allowing users to adjust the segmentation parameters and view the results in real-time. The paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of EdgeFlow, demonstrating its effectiveness on a variety of image datasets and use cases. Overall, EdgeFlow represents a significant advancement in the field of interactive segmentation, providing a practical and efficient solution for a wide range of applications.

row.title: EdgeFlow: Achieving Practical Interactive Segmentation with Edge-Guided Flow
row.prompt: Write the abstract for the academic paper titled "EdgeFlow: Achieving Practical Interactive Segmentation with Edge-Guided Flow".
row.generation: The task of segmenting objects within an image requires a comprehensive understanding of spatial relationships between different segments. Traditional interactive semantic segmentation methods usually rely on global changes to images or regions, which may be detrimental to maintaining local context and relationship between adjacent pixel groups. In this work, we introduce a novel approach called EdgeFlow that uses edge information as input to achieve practical interactive segmentation while considering the local dependencies in real-time. Our proposed framework learns robust edge maps from both low and high resolution levels, utilizing temporal correlations through dynamic motion estimates based on optical flow. We then combine edge cues from high and low resolution level with a set of locally-adapted filter weights to create a fine-tuned intermediate map, capturing the delicate details across space and time. Finally, our model performs interactive manipulation using gradient descent until convergence, resulting in accurate segmentation output without the need for human intervention. Furthermore, we evaluate our method on three benchmark datasets, demonstrating outperformances over classical approaches by preserving more detailed spatial patterns while achieving significantly faster processing times.

row.title: Semi-supervised Contrastive Learning for Label-efficient Medical Image Segmentation
row.prompt: Write the abstract for the academic paper titled "Semi-supervised Contrastive Learning for Label-efficient Medical Image Segmentation".
row.generation: Semi-supervised contrastive learning (SSL) has emerged as a promising approach for medical image segmentation, where labeled data is scarce. In this paper, we propose a novel SSL framework for label-efficient medical image segmentation. Our approach leverages the inherent spatial and temporal correlations in medical images to learn a contrastive representation that can accurately segment the target organs. We evaluate our method on three benchmark datasets and demonstrate state-of-the-art performance with significantly fewer labeled examples than previous methods. Our approach has the potential to revolutionize medical image segmentation by enabling more efficient and accurate diagnosis and treatment planning.

row.title: Semi-supervised Contrastive Learning for Label-efficient Medical Image Segmentation
row.prompt: Write the abstract for the academic paper titled "Semi-supervised Contrastive Learning for Label-efficient Medical Image Segmentation".
row.generation: Semi-supervised learning is a powerful approach that can improve medical image segmentation performance while reducing the amount of labeled data required. In this study, we propose a semi-supervised contrastive learning framework that enhances label efficiency by jointly training both pixel and feature distribution across multiple categories for medical image segmentation tasks. Specifically, our method leverages adversarial and mutual information losses to align semantic representations between unlabeled images and their corresponding ground truths in an iterative process. Using this optimization strategy, we demonstrate state-of-the-art results on several benchmark datasets with significantly fewer labeled examples than prior methods. Our approach represents a significant advancement towards building robust and efficient deep learning models for medical image segmentation tasks while minimizing human intervention.

row.title: Combo Loss: Handling Input and Output Imbalance in Multi-Organ Segmentation
row.prompt: Write the abstract for the academic paper titled "Combo Loss: Handling Input and Output Imbalance in Multi-Organ Segmentation".
row.generation: Multi-organ segmentation is a challenging task in medical image analysis, as it requires identifying multiple organs within a single image. However, one of the main challenges in this task is the imbalance between the number of input and output classes. This imbalance can lead to poor performance in the segmentation task, as the model tends to focus more on the majority class and neglect the minority classes. In this paper, we propose a new loss function called Combo Loss, which addresses this issue by combining two different loss functions: cross-entropy loss and Dice loss. The cross-entropy loss is used to penalize the model for incorrect predictions, while the Dice loss is used to penalize the model for poor overlap between the predicted and ground-truth segmentations. By combining these two loss functions, Combo Loss is able to better handle input and output imbalance in multi-organ segmentation tasks. We evaluate Combo Loss on several benchmark datasets and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to class imbalance.

row.title: Combo Loss: Handling Input and Output Imbalance in Multi-Organ Segmentation
row.prompt: Write the abstract for the academic paper titled "Combo Loss: Handling Input and Output Imbalance in Multi-Organ Segmentation".
row.generation: Input and output imbalance is a common problem faced by many multi-organ segmentation tasks. This can occur when some organs are frequently occluded or have lower contrast than others, making it more difficult to accurately identify them in images. In this study, we propose a new loss function called combo loss that addresses both input and output imbalance. Combo loss is designed to incorporate feedback from both input and output branches of a typical encoder-decoder model for multi-organ segmentation. We demonstrate that our proposed approach significantly improves performance on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness for handling input and output imbalance in challenging multi-organ segmentation problems.

row.title: Attention-Based 3D Seismic Fault Segmentation Training by a Few 2D Slice Labels

The attention mechanism allows the model to focus on the most relevant 2D slices during training, reducing the number of required labels and improving the accuracy of the resulting 3D fault segmentation model. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated on a synthetic seismic dataset, where the model achieves state-of-the-art performance with only a small number of 2D slice labels.

row.title: Attention-Based 3D Seismic Fault Segmentation Training by a Few 2D Slice Labels

row.generation: The objective of this research is to use few labeled two-dimensional (2D) seismic slice data sets to train an attention-based convolutional neural network (CNN) on three-dimensional (3D) fault segmentations. In doing so, an end--end learning methodology with a modified encoder-decoder architecture has been adopted to classify 3D volumes based solely on limited input 2D labels while using spatial and temporal attention mechanisms to learn fault geometries across entire 3D space. Various evaluations have shown that our method can achieve comparable performance with larger labeled 2D datasets, even outperforming them in some cases, indicating the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Additionally, experiments from which CNN layer parameters were updated during training demonstrated superior performance over static models. Our results suggest that it may be feasible to develop effective 3D fault segmentation techniques utilizing small labeled datasets in a targeted manner, thereby reducing considerable costs associated with acquiring large labeled datasets and improving fault hazards mitigation assessments in oil and gas reservoirs.

row.title: Segmenter: Transformer for Semantic Segmentation

Segmenter: Transformer for Semantic Segmentation

In this paper, we present Segmenter, a novel deep learning model for semantic segmentation that utilizes a transformer architecture. The transformer architecture has shown great success in natural language processing tasks, but its effectiveness in image segmentation has not been fully explored. We propose a transformer-based model for semantic segmentation that can effectively capture long-range dependencies between pixels and improve the accuracy of segmentation.

Our model consists of an encoder-decoder architecture, where the encoder processes the input image and generates a sequence of feature vectors, and the decoder generates the segmentation mask based on these feature vectors. The transformer architecture is used in both the encoder and decoder to process the sequence of feature vectors. We also introduce a novel attention mechanism that allows the model to focus on the most relevant regions of the image during segmentation.

We evaluate our model on several benchmark datasets and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art models in terms of accuracy and speed. Our model is also able to handle complex scenes with multiple objects and backgrounds, making it a valuable tool for a wide range of applications.

Overall, our work demonstrates the effectiveness of transformer architectures in image segmentation and paves the way for further research in this area.

row.title: Segmenter: Transformer for Semantic Segmentation

Our empirical results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method on several benchmark tasks, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines while achieving significantly faster runtimes than previous transformer-based solutions.

Our approach leverages additional contextual information such as textual descriptions, 3D models, and user feedback to enhance the accuracy of semantic segmentation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on several benchmark datasets and show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art image-based semantic segmentation methods. Our work paves the way for more accurate and robust semantic segmentation in complex scenes.

row.title: Mining Contextual Information Beyond Image for Semantic Segmentation

Abstract:

Our approach is based on a novel combination of multi-task and generative models, where each region is predicted conditioned on both the image context and external sources of knowledge. We evaluate our proposed method on public benchmarks and demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, particularly when analyzing complex videos sequences. Overall, this research represents an initial step towards more realistic and interpretable modeling of visual content.

We validate our model's efficacy on multiple datasets with limited training data, demonstrating state-of-the-art results and outpacing prior methods in terms of accuracy, tradeoff between speed and quality, and generalization ability across unseen or challenging classes and scenes.

row.title: Iterative, Deep, and Unsupervised Synthetic Aperture Sonar Image Segmentation
row.prompt: Write the abstract for the academic paper titled "Iterative, Deep, and Unsupervised Synthetic Aperture Sonar Image Segmentation".
row.generation:
The field of underwater sound technology has seen a significant evolution in recent years with research focused on using sonar imaging to increase our understanding of marine environments. This study presents an iterative, deep, and unsupervised synthetic aperture sonar (SAS) image segmentation methodology that allows accurate and efficient classification of seafloor topography, sediment texture, and other marine organisms within sonar images.

The proposed method is based on two key components: feature extraction followed by an iterative neural network approach to segmentation. Feature extraction involves extracting specific information from the sonar images, such as texture, edge strength, and intensity at various frequency bands. The resulting extracted features are then fed into an unsupervised autoencoder that learns to represent each area in a sonnet-like sequence. The output generated is then used in conjunction with an additional neural network architecture to perform multi-layer perceptron (MLP)-based synthesis to produce high-resolution segmented versions of the sonar images.

Experimental results indicate improved accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional methods. The iterative, deep, and unsupervised SAS image segmentation technique developed provides a useful tool for researchers working towards more effective monitoring and management of ocean habitats, allowing them to identify changes over time and detect critical indicators of ecosystem health.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach for semantic image segmentation using double similarity distillation. Our method leverages the similarity between the input image and the teacher model's output, as well as the similarity between the teacher model's output and the student model's output, to improve the performance of the student model. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on several benchmark datasets, achieving state-of-the-art results in some cases. Our approach can be easily integrated into existing semantic segmentation models, making it a valuable tool for improving the performance of these models.

row.title: Inter Extreme Points Geodesics for Weakly Supervised Segmentation

row.generation:
Inter Extreme Points (IEPs) provide a promising approach to weakly supervised image segmentation. IEPs are points in images that can be computed from a small region around them using geometric properties such as distance and angles, without requiring explicit object detection or pixel-level labeling. In our work, we explore their potential in weakly supervised automatic segmentation by analyzing their structural relationships with local neighbors and other regions within an image.

We show that IEPs possess rich information about object boundaries, shape, texture, and contextual hierarchy, which makes them well suited for weak supervision. However, direct use of IEPs is limited by their low resolution compared with pixels, leading to spatial ambiguity. To address this limitation, we propose a novel framework that constructs intermediate representations between spatial neighborhoods and pixels based on smooth 3-D geodetic paths connecting extreme points across regions with similar geometric structures. Our scheme explicitly exploits spatial continuity, while preserving local geometric relationships among elements in these regions.

Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of intermediate levels of supervisory information using IEPs to improve accuracy for both unsupervised and semi-supervised image segmentation tasks. It also enables visualization of underlying image structure through analysis of IEP cluster connectivity patterns. Overall, our proposed method offers new insights into interpreting spatial hierarchy and integrating nonlocal features at various scales and resolutions for weakly supervised image processing in computer vision applications.

Abstract:

Our model leverages the power of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to learn and extract features from images, and then employs a novel multi-task learning framework to simultaneously perform object detection, semantic segmentation, and instance segmentation. By integrating these three tasks into a unified model, K-Net is able to achieve state-of-the-art performance on various benchmark datasets, while also reducing the computational complexity and memory requirements compared to existing models. Furthermore, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by applying it to real-world scenarios, such as medical image analysis and autonomous driving. Overall, K-Net represents a significant step towards achieving unified image segmentation, and paves the way for future research in this area.
